[[Category:Artificial neural network]][[Category:Special function]]
An '''activation function''' is a mathematical [[function]].

It is part of layer-to-layer '''feedforward mechanisms''' of an [[artificial neural network (ANN)]].

* For a simple [[ANN]],the [[feedforward algorithm]]
* For a [[Transformer]], the [[feed-Forward Network (FFN) Sub-Layer (Transformer)|Feed-Forward Network (FFN)]]

== Formal definition ==

An activation function is any component-wise real-vector map

$$
\sigma:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n
$$

so for any $\vec z = (z_1,z_2,\dots,z_n)$:

$$
\sigma(\vec z)=(\sigma(z_1),\sigma(z_2),\dots,\sigma(z_n))
$$

== Importance ==

'''Without''' an activation function:

$$
\mathbf{W}_2\left(\mathbf{W}_1\vec x+\vec b_1\right)+\vec b_2
=
\mathbf{W}\vec x+\vec b,
\qquad
\mathbf{W}=\mathbf{W}_2\mathbf{W}_1,
\quad
\vec b=\mathbf{W}_2\vec b_1+\vec b_2,
$$

Hence, any number of layers of [[artificial neuron]]s is strictly equivalent to 1 larger layer, a phenomenon known as '''depth collapse'''.

The activation function, which introduces '''non-linearity''', enables the preservation of depth of an [[ANN]].

== Common variants ==

* [[(leaky) rectified/exponential linear units (ReLU, LeakyReLU, ELU)]]
* [[sigmoid function]]
* [[sigmoid linear unit (SLU)]]
* [[gated linear unit (GLU)]]
* [[hyperbolic tangent]]
* [[Gaussian error linear unit (GeLU)]]
